title: Ready to eat, unable to ululate
odia:
ଖାଇଲା ବେଳକୁ ସାତ ପୁଅ ମା
ହୁଳହୁଳି ଦେଲା ବେଳକୁ ଜିଭରେ ଘା।
literal_meaning: At eating time, a mother of seven sons; at ululation time, a sore on the tongue.
meaning_odia: ଖାଇବା ବେଳେ ସାତ ପୁଅର ମା, ହୁଳହୁଳି ଦେବା ବେଳେ ଜିଭରେ ଘା—ଏହି ଦୁଇ ଅବସ୍ଥାକୁ ଯୋଡ଼ି କଥାଟି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କରେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ନିଜେ ସୁବିଧା ଭୋଗ କରିବାକୁ ଆଗ୍ରହ, କିନ୍ତୁ ନିଜ ଭାଗର ସହଯୋଗ ଦେବା ବେଳେ ଅସୁବିଧା ଦେଖାଇବା ପ୍ରତି ଇଙ୍ଗିତ ଅଛି।
explanation: The two occasions expose a change in readiness: the first announces a mother of seven sons at mealtime, while the second produces a tongue too sore for an ululating cry. Our editorial reading hears a complaint about enjoying the benefits while finding an obstacle when participation is expected. The joke lies in the convenient contrast between the two moments.
usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone eagerly joins a shared meal but repeatedly withdraws when the group asks for help preparing its next gathering. Another participant quotes the saying about willingness that changes with the occasion.
cultural_context: The repeated ବେଳକୁ sets the occasions side by side. Eating and ululating both involve the mouth, making the tongue’s sudden prominence in the second line pointed. The literal mother-of-seven image lends the opening an expansive tone before the short complaint about a sore closes it.
